Question 1
?

Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of ln⁡(x+1) about x=0.

a
x−x2+23x3−34x4
b
x−x2+23x3−14x4
c
x−12x2+13x3−14x4
d
x−12x2+13x3−34x4
e
x−12x2+14x3−13x4
Submit

decision.explanation: The Maclaurin series is ln(1+x)=x−x²/2+x³/3−x⁴/4+⋯. Keeping terms through degree four gives option c.

a

EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by

P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=0, so

P4(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)2!x2+f‴(0)3!x3+f(4)(0)4!x4.

So we need to work out f(0), f′(0), f″(0), f‴(0) and f(4)(0) as follows: f(x)=ln⁡(x+1)⟹f(0)=ln⁡(0+1)=0f′(x)=1x+1⟹f′(0)=10+1=1f″(x)=−1(x+1)2⟹f″(0)=−1(0+1)2=−1f‴(x)=2(x+1)3⟹f‴(0)=2(0+1)3=2f(4)(x)=−6(x+1)4⟹f(4)(0)=−6(0+1)4=−6

Therefore, P4(x) is given by

P4(x)=0+1⋅x+(−1)2!x2+23!x3+(−6)4!x4=x−12x2+13x3−14x4.

decision.explanation: Let h=x−π. Then cos²(x)=cos²(h)=(1+cos(2h))/2. Expanding through degree four gives 1−h²+h⁴/3, which matches option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of ${cos}^{2}⁡(x)$ about $x=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^{4}.
$$

Here, we have $a=\pi ,$ so

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(\pi )+{f}^{′}(\pi )(x-\pi )+\frac{{f}^{″}(\pi )}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\pi )}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\pi )}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.
$$

So we need to work out $f(\pi ),$ ${f}^{′}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{″}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{‴}(\pi )$ and ${f}^{(4)}(\pi ),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\pi ) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(\pi )=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\pi ) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=-2 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\pi ) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\pi ) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${P}_{4}(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =1+(0)(x-\pi )+\frac{(-2)}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{8}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4} \\  & =1-{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of ${cos}^{2}⁡(x)$ about $x=\pi .$
content.worked_solution:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^{4}.
$$

Here, we have $a=\pi ,$ so

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(\pi )+{f}^{′}(\pi )(x-\pi )+\frac{{f}^{″}(\pi )}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\pi )}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\pi )}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.
$$

So we need to work out $f(\pi ),$ ${f}^{′}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{″}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{‴}(\pi )$ and ${f}^{(4)}(\pi ),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\pi ) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(\pi )=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\pi ) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=-2 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\pi ) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\pi ) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${P}_{4}(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =1+(0)(x-\pi )+\frac{(-2)}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{8}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4} \\  & =1-{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
